correctness.rationale: The graph and exact switch rule are explicit. Exhaustive anchored DFS visits each of the 1280 undirected Hamiltonian tours exactly once. Any legal two-edge switch is exactly the four-edge symmetric difference with a host-graph 4-cycle; checking membership in the enumerated tours excludes disconnected 2-factors. All 30 four-cycles and 1800 switches are exhaustively tested. A second implementation constructs the 20 graph faces and actual vertex-order two-opt reversals, independently reproducing every state and transition. Explicit BFS gives 30 components of size 36, 60 of size 2, 80 isolates; all large components have 58 edges and diameter 8. A separate backtracking enumeration of all 120 graph automorphisms proves the component-orbit classification.

originality.rationale: The exact two-edge Hamiltonian-switch definition matches Takaoka (2018), but that paper proves general hardness and connectivity only for specified graph classes, not the complete icosahedral transition graph. Hopkins (2004) classifies Platonic Hamiltonian cycles by topological symmetry rather than single-switch connectivity. The MathOverflow (2010-2011) count of 512 undirected cycles through a fixed edge implies the known global count 1280, which is not claimed novel; it does not determine the new 170-component decomposition or the four component symmetry orbits. Targeted literature and mathematical-record comparisons found no covering theorem or table. Priority risk from unindexed work remains.
residual_risks: An earlier unpublished, unindexed, or differently named exact two-opt adjacency enumeration of the icosahedron could predate this calculation.

value.rationale: The natural switch graph for Hamiltonian tours is a classical combinatorial reconfiguration object. On the maximally symmetric icosahedron, 170 disconnected components, 80 immovable cycles, and 60 isolated pairs exhibit a substantive obstruction to standard two-opt reachability. The 30 isomorphic 36-state components and complete component-orbit classification explain accessibility rather than merely providing another known tour count; the full certificate is reusable for comparisons in Hamiltonian reconfiguration theory.
